data.one_liner: Check app version against app stores or remote JSON and display update dialogs.
data.what_it_does: Checks the currently installed app version against the Apple App Store, Google Play Store, or a custom remote JSON config. Provides built-in presentation layers like Material/Cupertino dialogs, bottom sheets, full-screen pages, and an UpdateGate widget to handle force updates and smart snooze.
use_when: You need to enforce minimum app versions or prompt users for soft updates.
You want to query App Store and Google Play directly without setting up a backend.
You want a declarative widget wrapper to check updates automatically on startup and resume.
avoid_when: Your app is deployed exclusively via enterprise or private distribution channels that lack store lookups or custom JSON configuration.
You want completely custom state management for update flows rather than the library's built-in dialogs and logic.
strengths: Zero-backend store lookup directly from Apple App Store and Google Play Store.
Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, Web, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Includes declarative UpdateGate widget with lifecycle check-on-resume support.
Smart snooze and skip-version logic to reduce update fatigue.
weaknesses: Relies on scraping store pages or third-party store metadata which can occasionally break if stores change their layout.
Limited to update checking and built-in UI prompts.
